d.t: A period of time akin to the time taken for the Earth to undergo a full cycle of seasons.
d.e: we moved to this town a year ago; I quit smoking exactly one year ago

d.t: (by extension) An orbital period: the period of one revolution in any particular orbit: The time it takes for any astronomical object (such as a planet, dwarf planet, small Solar System body, or comet) in direct orbit around a star (such as the Sun) to make one revolution around the star.
d.e: Mars goes around the sun once in a Martian year, or 1.88 Earth years.

d.t: A period between set dates that mark a year, such as from January 1 to December 31 by the Gregorian calendar, from Tishri 1 to Elul 29 by the Jewish calendar, and from Muharram 1 to Dhu al-Hijjah 29 or 30 by the Islamic calendar.
d.e: A normal year has 365 full days, but there are 366 days in a leap year.

d.t: A scheduled part of a calendar year spent in a specific activity.
d.e: During this school year I have to get up at 6:30 to catch the bus.

d.t: The proportion of a creature's lifespan equivalent to one year of an average human lifespan (see also dog year).
d.e: Geneticists have created baker's yeast that can live to 800 in yeast years.

d.t: Pronunciation spelling of here.
Pronunciation spelling of hear.
Used to show agreement or acceptance.
d.e: Yes, you are correct.

d.t: Used to indicate disagreement or dissent in reply to a negative statement.
d.e:
It was not my fault we lost the race.
Oh, yes, it was!

d.t: (humorous) Answer to a question presuming one answer when all answers are correct.
d.e:
Do you like cake, or pie?
Yes.

d.t: An exclamation of pleasure or approval, usually transcribed with an exclamation point.
d.e: Our second goal of the match! Yes!

d.t: Response that confirms that the user is paying attention.
(interrogative) Used to ask for more information with a request.
d.e:
I need some help.
Yes?

d.t: An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.
d.e: Was that a yes?

d.t: A vote of support or in favor of something.
d.e: The workers voted on whether to strike, and there were thirty "yeses" and one "no".

d.t: (colloquial, transitive) To agree with, affirm, approve.
d.e: Did he yes the veto?

d.t: (colloquial, intransitive) To say “yes”.
(slang) To attempt to flatter someone by habitually agreeing
(humorous) Countering a statement using the determiner no:
(object pronoun) The people spoken, or written to, as an object.
d.e: Both of you should get ready now.

d.t: (reflexive pronoun, now US colloquial) (To) yourselves, (to) yourself.
(object pronoun) The person spoken to or written to, as an object. (Replacing thee; originally as a mark of respect.)
(subject pronoun) The people spoken to or written to, as a subject. (Replacing ye.)
d.e: You are all supposed to do as I tell you.

d.t: (subject pronoun) The person spoken to or written to, as a subject. (Originally as a mark of respect.)
(subject pronoun, colloquial) A person's favorite sports team.
d.e: I get that you're from Southeast Michigan, but I'm still surprised that you're a Detroit Lions fan. You have been on the receiving end of losing seasons for a while now.

d.t: (indefinite personal pronoun) Anyone, one; an unspecified individual or group of individuals (as subject or object).

(indefinite personal pronoun) A dummy pronoun used in certain constructions, usually with verbs of receiving (such as get or find) or sensing (such as see or hear), typically stating the existence or typicality of something.
d.e: You get a lot of rude people in London.

d.t: The individual or group spoken or written to.
d.e: Have you gentlemen come to see the lady who fell backwards off a bus?

d.t: Used before epithets, describing the person being addressed, for emphasis.
d.e: You idiot!

d.t: (nonstandard) Your.
(transitive) To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).
The name of the Latin script letter U/u.
In the early part of growth or life; born not long ago.
d.e: a lamb is a young sheep

d.t: At an early stage of existence or development; having recently come into existence.
d.e: the age of space travel is still young

d.t: (Not) advanced in age; (far towards or) at a specified stage of existence or age.
d.e:
And thou, our Mother, twice two centuries young,
Bend with bright shafts of truth thy bow fresh-strung.

d.t: Junior (of two related people with the same name).
Early (of a decade of life).
d.e:
1922, E. Barrington, “The Mystery of Stella” in “The Ladies!” A Shining Constellation of Wit and Beauty, Boston: Atlantic Monthly Press, pp. 40-41,
[…] Miss Hessy is as pretty a girl as eye can see, in her young twenties and a bit of a fortune to boot.

d.t: Youthful; having the look or qualities of a young person.
d.e: My grandmother is a very active woman and is quite young for her age.

d.t: Of or belonging to the early part of life.
d.e: The cynical world soon shattered my young dreams.

d.t: (obsolete) Having little experience; inexperienced; unpracticed; ignorant; weak.
(often as if a plural noun) Offspring, especially the immature offspring of animals.
d.e: The lion caught a gnu to feed its young.

d.t: (informal or demography) To become or seem to become younger.
(informal or demography) To cause to appear younger.
(geology) To exhibit younging.
Belonging to you; of you; related to you (singular; one owner).
d.e: Let’s meet tomorrow at your convenience.

d.t: Belonging to you; of you; related to you (plural; more owners).
A determiner that conveys familiarity and mutual knowledge of the modified noun.
d.e: Not your average Tom, Dick and Harry.

d.t: (Ireland) That; the specified (usually used with a human referent)
d.e: Your man just bought a new car.

d.t: Misspelling of you're.
